default: It is six weeks since the ritual: the forty-fifth day.

default.text: The fountain in the market square runs some days. Today is one of them. It is a thin stream, clear and cold, and nobody quite trusts it yet.
default.else: The fountain in the market square is running again. It isn't running strongly. It is a thin stream, more a matter of principle than anything to cheer about. But the water is clear and cold, and it comes out of the ground without the wrongness the well water had.

default: Somebody put a cup on the fountain's edge. Then somebody else put another cup. By the end of the day there are seven cups, and a child is drinking out of one of them.
You and [missing person] watch from the other side of the square. Neither of you says anything.

default.text: Wren is at the fountain with a cup. He fills it and gives it to the child, and goes back for another.
In the end the two men from the gate were sent on to the capital under escort. The woman stayed. She keeps the ledger at the post now, because nobody else wanted to.

text.commander:
Vorne leaves on the forty-third day. He takes twenty-two soldiers and leaves six: on paper a garrison, in practice hardly more than a flag.

He shakes your hand before he goes, and [missing person]'s. He shakes Maret's hand too, which plainly costs them both something, but they manage it.

He doesn't shake Pol's hand, and Pol doesn't offer it. They stand together for a moment and look at each other, two people who dealt with the same trouble in different ways and are deciding what to make of that.

Then Vorne goes. The six who are left behave themselves and make themselves useful, and nobody much minds them.
text.arcane:
The account has been better received than you ever expected.

Two universities have written asking for the whole of it. A colleague in the capital has proposed a gathering of scholars, the first time anybody will have sat down formally to discuss the curse as a thing that is known and written down. And somebody you have never heard of, in a city a long way off, has written to say they have been studying something like it and may have evidence that bears on it.

Ashenveld is no longer a mystery off by itself. It has a name, and a place in what the world knows about itself.

You sit in the Tallow reading the letters, and [missing person] sits across from you doing something with their hands. It is the knot Lira taught them, the same ward knot. It is a perfectly ordinary moment, and you find that remarkable.
text.ranger:
Six weeks.

The hawk you first saw on the thirtieth day has a territory now. You can make out its habits from the market square. It hunts the north end of the ordinary forest from early morning until the middle of the morning, and rests, and hunts again in the late afternoon.

That tells you something about the hawk. It also tells you something about Ashenveld. The hawk has decided to have a territory here. It has decided there is enough food to keep it, and that this is a place worth staying.

You write it down: the forty-fifth day, the hawk has a territory.
text.cipher:
Six weeks, and things have settled into a shape that should hold for some time.

The Compact keeps a presence here, a small one, mostly clerks. The Covenant has a smaller place too, but an honest one, looking after its people. The Rootless camp has become the thing that matters most to how Ashenveld actually mends, which is where it ought to be.

Nobody got all they wanted. What you have is a compromise people can live with, and that is the best that politics ever gives you. It isn't a triumph, or justice. It is a state of affairs in which the people who need to get on with things can get on with them.

You look at what you have built, and decide it will do. It was all you were aiming for. You aren't sure when you decided that, but you did.

choices.text: Look honestly at what the six weeks have done.

default.text:
You and [missing person] sit by the fountain in the market square, running again, and go over it honestly.

The ritual stopped the curse spreading. The afflicted are no worse, and some of them are measurably better. The worst of it, the ruins and the people who went furthest in, will take longer, perhaps a great deal longer.

The six weeks have given Ashenveld an arrangement that works, to go on mending by. They have given it an account that will outlast everyone in this square. And they have made the Rootless camp the centre of whatever happens next.

As for what the two of you have lost and gained yourselves, there is too much of it for one afternoon by a fountain, and you both know it.

[missing person] watches the child with the cup for a while. "I should do it again," they say.

"I know," you say.

default: It is six weeks since you left Ashenveld.

You have come to a town [missing person] decided they wanted to see. It has nothing to do with anything that went before. Somebody told them the market here is good, and the rooms are cheap, and there are birds in the forest to the north that they haven't seen for fourteen months.
That is how they find their way now: towards birds, and markets people speak well of, and rooms in towns they have never been to.
You find your way with them. It is a different skill, you are discovering, from the ones you learned in Ashenveld. You read less for damage, and more for what might be.

default.text: It has happened twice more since. Both times you were awake.

text.commander:
A fortnight ago a letter came from Cael. The account has arrived, Vorne has finished withdrawing, and the Rootless camp has been formally recognised.

You read it, sent a short reply that confirmed things and said nothing else, and put it away.

The work is done. You never needed telling so. That it is done is what you wanted, and it has happened, and here you are in a town with a good market and cheap rooms, which is another kind of achievement.
text.arcane:
The letters from other scholars follow you about. That is all right. It is the work you were made for, and it doesn't need you to be anywhere in particular.

You write to your colleagues from a table in a market town, and the letters they get have the name of the town at the top, and none of them thinks it odd, because scholars move about and the work moves with them.

[missing person] watches you write and asks, "Is it strange? Doing this from here?"

"No," you say, and mean it. "This is what the work looks like when there isn't a crisis."

They think about it. "I think I like it better," they say.
text.ranger:
There are birds in the forest to the north that you haven't seen for weeks. [missing person] was right about that.

You spend an afternoon in the forest reading it, not for damage done by the curse, or for how fast it is mending, but simply because it is interesting. You had forgotten that it could be.
text.cipher:
Six weeks out, and the person beside you has become the easiest person to read you have ever known.

It comes of the ritual, and the ruins, and of having had everything in you looked at by something that missed nothing. You know them entirely, and they know you. There is nothing left to keep back.

What you are finding is that knowing somebody entirely does not stop them being interesting. If anything, it is only then that you begin to be interested in what they will do with what they are.

Either that is a great piece of wisdom, or it is simply what it is like to be in love with somebody who has lately spent fourteen months in a ruined city. You haven't decided which.

choices.text: Decide what comes next. Not Ashenveld. What comes after it.

default.text:
You sit down together and decide.

It isn't a grand plan. It is a direction, something to go towards instead of something to get away from. It makes use of what the two of you became in Ashenveld, in a way that has nothing to do with Ashenveld.

What matters is that it is decided, and that you decided it together, and that when you get up from the table and go out into the market town, you are both going the same way.

Ashenveld is behind you, but what you learned there isn't.

choices.text: Turn back, and walk east again together.

default.text: You don't decide it so much as notice that it has been decided. One morning you turn round on the road, and [missing person] turns with you, and neither of you says why.

default: You have been six weeks alone in Ashenveld.
On the forty-fifth day you take stock.

The Rootless camp is the strongest thing in Ashenveld's recovery, and Maret is the most important person in the region. Branch has learned to do some of what you do. Lira is getting better, slowly and unevenly, but she is getting better.
The Watcher from the gate is at the camp. He has his name back now: Joren. You found it in the old man's papers from Harrow. He answers to it sometimes, not always, but sometimes.
You had a hand in all of it. Everyone here did, but you stayed, and put yourself to the work, and that counts for something.
In the sixth week Maret finds you in the garden with a folded paper in her hand. It is the list. It has gone soft.
"Keep it," she says. "I am afraid that one morning I will forget it matters. If you have it, somebody will remember."
text.commander:
Vorne's offer still stands. You have been thinking about it for a month.

A post in the government of the region would give you a long reach, and it would tie your hands as well. The reach would be useful, and the ties would be real.

You make up your mind. You will tell Vorne tomorrow.

What you have decided is your own business.
text.arcane:
You have built things in Ashenveld that will go on without you if you leave: the watch on the curse, the account, and what you have made with Pol and Branch and Lira.

You have built something in yourself, too, that will go with you wherever you go: what you know of what the ritual needed, what the mechanism showed you, and what it is to be seen entirely by something that does not judge.
text.ranger:
The hawk has a territory. The fountain is running. Twice in the last fortnight Lira has gone to the market alone and come back with things she wanted, rather than things she needed.

The world is mending, and you are part of the reason.

You think about the one you let go, and the letter you wrote, and the letters they have written back, ordinary and warm, about places you have never been.

You think about all that, and then you go to see Joren, because he is here, and needs somebody to look in on him, and today that is what there is to do.
text.cipher:
Six weeks alone, and if you are honest about it, this is how it stands.

You are not unhappy. That was the first surprise.

You are doing work that matters, with people you think well of, in a place that matters. The one who isn't here is not here, and that is real, and it sits alongside all the rest.

The second surprise is that you haven't finished with Ashenveld. You thought you might, one day. You haven't. There is more work here than you can do, and you have decided that is a good problem to have.

default.text:
You take it. She watches it go into your coat, and lets out a breath.

"The first one," she says. "Read me the first one at new moon. That is all."

choices.text: Tell her to keep it. It's hers.

default.text:
"It's yours," you say. "You won't forget it matters. You wrote it down."

She looks at the paper a long while, and then puts it back inside her coat.

choices.text: Take stock honestly, of everything gained and everything lost.

default.text:
On a cold afternoon in the sixth week you sit in Pol's herb garden, which grows far better than it ought to, and take stock of all of it.

You have the work, and the people, and the place, and something real that you helped to make.

You have lost, or chosen, or put aside, the one who isn't here, and the life you would have had if you had followed them west.

Pol comes out of the camp and sits down beside you without asking. She has been doing it for six weeks, sitting beside you when you need somebody there and never asking what you need.

"It'll do," you say, not quite to her.

"Yes," she says. "It will have to."
